questions.question_text: A 44 year old woman is terrified of heights. She develops a sense of vertigo even at 1st or 2nd floor of a building and avoids high rise buildings at all cost. The company she is working for undergoes relocation and she is required now to work at 15th floor of a building in central London. Which of the following is the best treatment option for her?
questions.explanation: Simple phobias such as acrophobia can be treated with the behavioural technique of systematic desensitization.

questions.question_text: A 40-year-old man who works for the state as a highway and bridge designer becomes extremely anxious when he has to drive across any bridge. Which technique can best help him?
questions.explanation: Systematic desensitization can reduce anxiety in a situation by identifying a hierarchy of situations that produce anxiety from low to high. For example, the bridge designer can be taught progressive muscle relaxation until he is as relaxed as possible, at which point he will begin by driving across the shortest or least anxiety-producing bridge (in vivo exposure). As he successfully experiences crossing the lowest anxiety-producing bridge, he can proceed up the hierarchy of bridges until he masters crossing the most anxiety-producing bridge.

questions.question_text: Which of the following behavioural treatment is useful in trichotillomania?
questions.explanation: Habit reversal training (HRT) is a behavioral treatment package useful in tics and other OCD spectrum disorders such as trichotillomania, nail biting, thumb sucking, and skin picking, etc.

questions.question_text: Which of the following correctly describes the exposure and response prevention treatment for a lady with fear of contamination and repeated washing?

options.text: Therapist asks her too limit her washing to 4 times per act
Therapist asks her to wash her hands without touching the dirt
Therapist asks her to say 'STOP' aloud whenever the fear of contamination is
Therapist asks her to touch the dirty linen but prevents her from washing her hands

correct_answer.text: Therapist asks her to touch the dirty linen but prevents her from washing her hands

questions.explanation: By asking the patient to touch the linen, the therapist is exposing her to obsession-inducing situations only to prevent the response of hand washing later.

questions.question_text: The increase in recall of the perceived threat of a natural disaster over time is associated with

options.text: Lack of improvement in PTSD over time

correct_answer.text: Lack of improvement in PTSD over time

questions.explanation: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) diagnosis often depends on a retrospective, self-report of exposure to a life-threatening event. Recalled threat intensity generally increases from the time of trauma. This amplification in recall intensity is associated with lack of PTSD symptom improvement.Heir et al. The British Journal of Psychiatry (2009) 194: 510-514

questions.question_text: Marked out of 1.00 A lady comes to your outpatient unit with a diagnosis of OCD made by her GP. Which of the following Classification symptoms is most likely in this patient?
questions.explanation: Checking is one of the most common features of OCD. It is more common than other symptoms listed in this question.

questions.explanation: Panic attacks cannot be unilateral. They are associated with a generalised autonomic activity and not directly related to cortical seizures that could be unilateral.

questions.question_text: A 25-year-old man has experienced an irrational fear of darkness since childhood. He is not distressed by this currently and does not take special measures to avoid dark spaces. Which of the following is true?

options.text: He has a specific phobia as he has an irrational fear
He has no specific phobia as fear of darkness is common
He has a specific phobia with loss of insight
He has no specific phobia as he does not have an avoidance behaviour
He has a specific phobia as he has it since childhood

correct_answer.text: He has no specific phobia as he does not have an avoidance behaviour

questions.explanation: Specific phobias are restricted to highly specific situations such as proximity to certain animals, natural phenomenon such as heights, thunder, darkness, flying, being trapped in closed spaces, urinating or defecating in public toilets, eating certain foods, dentistry, or the sight of blood or injury. The trigger is often discrete, but symptoms of anxiety are similar to panic attacks seen in other anxiety disorders

questions.question_text: For four weeks after an automobile accident where her husband died in front of her, a schoolteacher suffers from insomnia, poor concentration and tearfulness. She has nightmares and emotional outbursts when awake. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Acute stress reaction: starts usually in an hour; resolution starts within 8 hours if the stress is 'hit and run' type or 48 hours if it is prolonged. The presence of physical exhaustion, organic factors or disease states increases the risk. The stressor is usually one that poses a serious threat to security, integrity and social position. The patient may initially be dazed with narrowed attention; disorientation is not uncommon as a result. Sometimes agitation and overactivity are seen. Partial or complete amnesia for the acute stress reaction is not unheard of. Dissociative symptoms seem to predominate in some.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding PTSD is true?

options.text: Specific EEG changes occur in chronic PTSD
Previous history of neurotic illness precludes the development of PTSD features
PTSD symptoms usually occur within 6 months of the perceived trauma
Autonomic hyperarousal symptoms are usually rare

correct_answer.text: PTSD symptoms usually occur within 6 months of the perceived trauma

questions.explanation: PTSD symptoms usually occur within 6 months of the perceived trauma. The essential features are autonomic hyperarousal, re-experiencing of aspects of the stressful event and active avoidance of cues that remind of the trauma. Anhedonia may also be seen; dramatic acute bursts of anxiety may present as exaggerated startle and hyperarousal. Insomnia is common. Predisposing factors include maladaptive personality traits (e.g. anankastic) or previous history of neurotic illnesses.

questions.question_text: Obsessional slowness is common in which of the following type of obsessions?
questions.explanation: An obsessive need for symmetry and exactness and a compulsion to order and arrange often results in slowness

questions.question_text: A middle-aged woman suffers a panic attack and believes she is going to die. Which term could be used to describe this psychopathology?
questions.explanation: Outcome fear is a diagnostic feature of panic disorder. The bias in information processing that leads to outcome fear is termed as catastrophic misinterpretation.

questions.question_text: A patient with OCD has intrusive thoughts about the safety of his family. He fights these thoughts by often tapping his desk 5 times and also by praying mentally 5 times as fast as he could. The acts of praying are best termed as
questions.explanation: Compulsions are, in fact, merely obsessional motor acts. They may result from an obsessional impulse that leads directly to the action, or they may be mediated by an obsessional mental image or thought, as, for example, when the obsessional fear of contamination leads to compulsive washing.

questions.question_text: Mark Thurston came back from an army tour three months ago, where he was involved in front-line conflict and exposed to situations in which he witnessed others being subject to major injury. For the past six weeks, he's been experiencing PTSD symptoms, with particularly disturbed sleep. Which of the following would benefit Mr. Thurston the most in relation to his PTSD and sleep disturbance?

options.text: Increasing the length of stage 3 and 4 sleep
Increasing the number of non-REM sleep cycles
Reducing the amount of waking from REM sleep

questions.explanation: REM sleep disruption is implicated in PTSD, mediated by sympathetic system over-activity. REM sleep starts when the sympathetic nervous system and noradrenaline secretion are at their lowest level. Prazosin helps restore REM sleep cycles, which may help alleviate sleep disturbance and nightmares in PTSD.
